subject: Data handling venues and cross-border transfer — prospect Q&A
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@blueharborhealth.com>

Cc: Michael Tran <michael.tran@blueharborhealth.com>
Date: 2026-11-16T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Quick Q — where is customer data actually processed?

Hi Ben,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — Blue Harbor's CTO asked for a short write-up on where payloads are executed and which third parties might see request data. Specifically:
- Regions/locations where inference runs for hosted customers (us-west/us-east/eu)
- Any cross-border hops (if a US customer’s call is processed in EU for fallback, etc.)
- A list of subprocessors involved in request execution and where they host infrastructure

Can you send a concise breakdown and any evidence we can share with security? If there’s a one-page map or CSV roster, that would be ideal.

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Morales
Head of Security & Compliance
Blue Harbor Health
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-16T11:50:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Quick Q — where is customer data actually processed?

Hi Elena — great question. Short answer up front: hosted requests for US customers are executed in US regions by default (primary: us-west-2, failover: us-east-1); we do not route US traffic to EU regions except in specific cross-region failover cases or when a customer explicitly requests EU execution.

I've attached a concise summary (residency_summary.pdf) that covers:
- Default execution regions by account region
- Typical cross-border scenarios and automated fallback behavior
- High-level subprocessor list (we'll follow up with a full roster)

We have Marissa on this thread to share a technical map and the subprocessors roster. Kim is cc'd for formal compliance statements (retention, deletion SLA, KMS).

Next steps: Marissa will drop the execution map and the subprocessor CSV; Kim can attach the DP annex and confirm deletion timelines. Happy to schedule a short walkthrough if that helps.

Best,
Ben

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@blueharborhealth.com>, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-17T08:35:00-08:00
Subject: Technical map + subprocessor roster

Hi Elena — following up with more detail. Key points:

1) Execution topology (hosted API)
- Primary region chosen by customer account setting; default mapping for Blue Harbor (US) is us-west-2.
- Stateless fronting (edge) accepts request, then routes to a regional inference cluster. Clusters run on dedicated instance pools per region.
- Failover: if regional capacity exhausted, routing policy is to failover to an alternate US region where possible (us-east-1). We do not failover to EU by default.

2) Cross-border transfer scenarios
- Control-plane metadata (account IDs, routing hints) may traverse our global control plane (encrypted in transit). Payloads and model inputs are routed into the selected regional cluster and are not routed across continents except when a customer selects an execution region in another geography or in configured multi-region replication.
- Transient hops: logs/metrics for observability may be aggregated via our telemetry pipeline; when required for debugging we can provide redacted traces.

3) Subprocessors (high-level)
- Cloud compute: public cloud IaaS providers (US regions only for your default)
- Networking/CDN: global edge provider (only metadata, not request bodies)
- Monitoring/telemetry: telemetry ingestion vendor (encrypted)

Attachments included: execution_map.svg (visual of routing), subprocessor_roster.csv (vendor, role, region). The CSV lists vendor names and the type of processing they perform; let me know if you need contracts or DPA addenda per vendor.

If you want a version of the map with Blue Harbor-specific pins (account-level), we can generate that for the security review.

Cheers,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference
[Attachments: execution_map.svg, subprocessor_roster.csv]
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@blueharborhealth.com>, ben.carter@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-18T10:22:00-08:00
Subject: Compliance notes — retention, deletion, KMS, and DP Annex

Hi Elena — adding formal statements you can include in your security pack: 

- Retention & Deletion: By default Redwood retains request payloads (transient cache) for up to 30 days to support debugging and model quality monitoring; customers can configure shorter retention or opt into automatic deletion on ingest. We also provide a per-account tombstoning API to purge cached prefixes immediately.

- Deletion SLA: For hosted accounts we commit to final deletion from hot storage within 30 days of a request and rot through backups within 90 days. We provide deletion evidence logs on request via our audit export process.

- Key management: Production data at rest is encrypted with customer-specific keys in our KMS; we integrate with customer-managed KMS (bring your own key) for Dedicated/Private deployments and with Redwood-managed KMS for hosted tiers. Key rotation and access controls are logged.

- SOC 2 & DP Annex: Attached is DP-Annex-A.pdf (excerpt of contractual commitments around subprocessors, export controls, and deletion). Our SOC 2 Type II report is available under NDA.

- EU Processing & On-prem options: we support account-level region pinning to EU regions for EU-only execution, and we offer Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments for regulated workloads (this ensures compute never leaves customer-controlled networks).

If Blue Harbor needs us to produce per-vendor contracts or a signed data processing addendum listing subprocessors, we can prepare that; please indicate which items you need (evidence pack, signed DPA, SOC2).

Best regards,
Kimberly Park
Head of Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: DP-Annex-A.pdf]

1) For EU-residency: can you confirm which EU regions you offer and whether logs/telemetry ever transit through non-EU infrastructure for EU-pinned accounts?
2) For the subprocessor CSV — can you indicate which vendors have access to raw request payloads vs. metadata only?

Blue Harbor will need: a) an account-level residency map, b) a signed DPA listing subprocessors and roles, and c) SOC2 access (NDA ok). If Private deployment is recommended for PHI workloads, please flag that.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

–Elena
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, kimberly.park@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Data handling venues and cross-border transfer — next steps

Elena — thanks for the clear ask. Quick answers and next actions: 

- EU regions: we support eu-west-1 and eu-central-1 for EU-pinned accounts. When an account is pinned to EU, telemetry aggregation still uses global ingestion but payloads and persistent storage are constrained to EU regions; we can provide a redacted telemetry flow diagram for your security team.
- Subprocessor access levels: Marissa will mark the CSV with 'payload_access' flags (yes/no). In short: compute vendors have access to payloads for execution, CDN/edge vendors see metadata only, telemetry ingestion vendors see hashed/redacted telemetry by default.

Next steps (proposed):
1) We will produce an account-level residency map for Blue Harbor (Marissa) — ETA 2 business days.
2) We will prepare a signed DPA that enumerates subprocessors and their roles (Kim) — ETA 3 business days after Andrea in Legal signs the template; we can start the NDA if you prefer.
3) SOC 2: we can provide access under NDA — I can route that immediately.

I'll create a secure folder with the artifacts and send a DocuSign link for a mutual NDA / DPA starter so we can share the SOC2 report and full vendor contracts. Let me know if a short call later this week to walk Blue Harbor's security team through the map would help.

Thanks,
Ben
